speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a skin condition on your left dorsal hand; could you describe how long you have had it and if it is itchy, painful, or oozing? Also, have you recently had any insect bites, contact with plants, or been in a wooded area?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of sun exposure, could you describe the appearance and color of the lesion on your left dorsal hand, and has it changed size or shape recently? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis (AK). The patient's description of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on sun-exposed skin (left dorsal hand) in an elderly individual is classic for AK. The mention of a urinary tract infection is unrelated to this dermatological finding. Given your history of sun exposure and the typical appearance, we can proceed with a clinical diagnosis, but if you have any uncertainty, a biopsy can confirm it.
